item.title: Tinubu expands 2027 campaign appearances to 19 states, FCT
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has expanded his planned appearances at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rallies from 12 states to 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The revised campaign timetable lists 20 locations where the president is expected to attend rallies between October 24, 2026, and January 13, 2027, according to TheCable, which reported that the schedule was released by APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka. The revised itinerary adds Katsina, Taraba, Abuja, Gusau, Owerri and Ilorin to the president’s initial campaign trail, while also incorporating Akwa Ibom, Jigawa and Kebbi, where he has already attended rallies. Tinubu was initially scheduled to attend rallies in only 12 states, with other party leaders expected to represent him at campaign events in the remaining states. However, he has made appearances in several states outside the original schedule. On November 6, the president visited Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, where he attended an APC rally and inaugurated projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration. He followed this with a campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on November 7. Tinubu also attended the party’s rallies in Dutse, Jigawa State, on November 10, and Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, on November 17. The revised timetable now formally includes the three states among the locations for his personal campaign appearances. Under the updated schedule, Tinubu is expected to attend rallies in Katsina on December 2, Kano on December 17, Jalingo on December 19, Abuja on December 21, Gusau on December 28 and Owerri on December 30. The president is also scheduled to visit Yola, Adamawa State, on January 4; Sokoto on January 5; Ilorin, Kwara State, on January 8; Asaba, Delta State, on January 11; and Lagos on January 13. Other states listed for his personal appearances include Kaduna, Oyo, Borno and Enugu. The revised timetable also changes the dates of some rallies in the original calendar. The Bauchi rally, initially scheduled for November 29 with Tinubu expected to attend, has been moved to December 1, although the new timetable does not indicate a presidential appearance. The Sokoto rally has been shifted from December 5 to January 5, 2027, while the Asaba rally moves from December 12 to January 11. The Lagos rally, expected to serve as the campaign’s major closing event, has also been rescheduled from January 9 to January 13. The updated calendar lists 37 rallies across the 36 states and the FCT, with Tinubu expected to personally attend 20 of them. The North-West has the highest number of states on the president’s revised campaign itinerary, with seven: Kaduna, Jigawa, Kebbi, Katsina, Kano, Zamfara and Sokoto. The North-East and South-South follow with three states each. The North-East states are Borno, Taraba and Adamawa, while the South-South states are Akwa Ibom, Rivers and Delta. item.title: Senate passes bills establishing research fund, granting medical college PhD powers
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has passed two bills seeking to provide a framework for research funding and expand postgraduate medical education in Nigeria. The bills are the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill, 2026, and the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, 2026. Both bills were passed on Wednesday after consideration of their provisions, clause by clause, at the Committee of the Whole and subsequent third reading. Their passage followed the presentation and consideration of reports by the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund, chaired by Senator Mohammed Dandutse (APC, Katsina South). Presenting the reports, Dandutse said the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill sought to establish a sustainable funding mechanism for research, development and innovation across the country. He said the proposed legislation also provided for the establishment of the National Council on Research and Innovation, which would provide strategic direction, policy oversight and supervision for Nigeria’s research agenda. According to him, the proposed fund would support research institutions and provide a dedicated funding framework for addressing the country’s development challenges. He added that the fund and the council would work together to strengthen Nigeria’s research, scientific, technological and innovation capabilities. On the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, Dandutse said the proposed amendment sought to expand the academic and institutional functions of the college. He explained that the amendment would empower the college to establish academic programmes and award Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees in specialised medical disciplines. The areas include clinical medicine, dentistry, basic medical sciences, pharmacology and other related fields. Dandutse further explained that the amendment would empower the college’s Senate to develop, administer and supervise the proposed doctoral programmes. He said the programmes would be subject to accreditation and regulation by the National Universities Commission (NUC) to ensure compliance with prescribed academic standards. According to him, the proposed changes are intended to provide a framework for advanced medical education, clinical research and specialised medical training in the country. item.title: World Bank threatened to cut Nigeria’s financing over subsidy — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has said the World Bank warned Nigeria that it would stop financing the country unless the Federal Government removed petrol subsidy. Fashola, who served as Minister of Power under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, made the disclosure on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He said the decision to remove the subsidy was not merely a policy choice, but was also influenced by legal provisions and Nigeria’s financial position at the time. Fashola urged Nigerians to revisit President Bola Tinubu’s inaugural address, arguing that public attention had focused largely on the declaration that “subsidy is gone” without sufficient consideration of other parts of the speech. He also cited the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), which he said provided for petroleum products to be sold at competitive market rates, arguing that the provision had implications for any move to reinstate subsidy. “The World Bank simply said, ‘We won’t finance your country again unless you remove subsidy.’ It was that simple,” he said. Fashola said the issue had been discussed during the previous administration, when he was a member of the Federal Executive Council, adding that Nigeria was spending close to 90 per cent of its revenue on debt servicing. He argued that the country could not afford to sustain the subsidy regime and challenged those advocating its restoration to explain how they intended to fund it. The former minister also asked political opponents of the Tinubu administration to explain how they would implement an alternative policy if elected, saying some politicians who had previously supported subsidy removal had changed their positions after it became unpopular. He said the Tinubu administration deserved commendation for maintaining the policy despite the economic difficulties it had imposed on Nigerians. “What this government deserves commendation for is not falling over on its word and saying, ‘Because the people like it, let’s bring it back.’ It was a road to perdition,” he said. Fashola, however, acknowledged that subsidy removal had affected household livelihoods and increased the cost of living, but said the government was introducing other measures to cushion the impact. He listed tax reforms, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), salary adjustments and compressed natural gas (CNG) initiatives among the measures being deployed to address the economic pressures. He also cited a decline in inflation from above 30 per cent to about 14 per cent, arguing that reversing the subsidy policy midway could disrupt the progress recorded. The former governor recalled the Subsidy Reinvestment and Empowerment Programme (SURE-P), introduced under former President Goodluck Jonathan, as an earlier attempt to manage the proceeds from subsidy removal. item.title: DSS challenges Atiku to prove it recruited protesters in Sokoto
item.description: …Says preliminary investigation found no evidence against operatives …Recalls rescuing ADC governorship candidate from attack The Department of State Services (DSS) has challenged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to provide concrete evidence to support his allegation that the agency recruited protesters to disrupt the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign rally in Sokoto State. The secret police said its preliminary investigation into the allegation failed to establish any evidence linking its operatives to the organisation or sponsorship of protests against the ADC’s campaign activities in the state. Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, had earlier accused the Sokoto State Government of obstructing his party’s campaign activities ahead of its rally in the state. Addressing journalists in Abuja, the former Vice-President also alleged that the DSS recruited protesters to cause unrest and create grounds for imposing a curfew that could prevent the opposition party from holding its rally as scheduled. However, in a statement issued on Tuesday, the Deputy Director of Public Relations and Strategic Communications of the DSS, Favour Dozie, said the agency activated its internal investigation procedures following the public allegation. Dozie said the investigation was conducted on the directive of the Director-General of the DSS, Adeola Ajayi, and involved interviews with ADC leaders in Sokoto, party members and other relevant stakeholders. According to the spokesperson, Atiku had specifically alleged that the ADC knew where some of the protesters were assembled and how they were allegedly deployed to strategic locations. Quoting the former Vice-President, Dozie said: “Where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road. Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout.” The DSS spokesperson, however, said the agency’s preliminary findings did not substantiate the allegation. “Outcome of the preliminary investigation did not confirm the allegation, as there was no evidence to establish such,” the statement said. In presenting its account of its activities in Sokoto, the agency recalled that on October 31, its operatives rescued Mannir Daniya, the ADC governorship candidate in the state, from an attack and evacuated him to safety. It said two of its operatives were assaulted during the rescue operation and were receiving medical attention at the time of its earlier statement. The agency further disclosed that Daniya subsequently contacted the State Director of the DSS to express appreciation for the intervention and request additional security reinforcement. It also said it received letters of appreciation from the ADC state chairman and the governorship candidate, describing the correspondence as evidence of its efforts to protect political actors irrespective of their party affiliations. item.title: Atiku questions Tinubu’s Villa interview over $4.5m US lobbying deal
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has questioned whether President Bola Tinubu’s recently recorded interview at the Presidential Villa was connected to a $4.5 million lobbying contract involving the Nigerian government in the United States. Atiku demanded that the Presidency disclose the terms of the contract, explain the purpose of the payment and release the full, unedited interview to establish whether the recording was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement. In a statement on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified Diana London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged to work for the Nigerian government through Aster Legal. He said the filings showed that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but did not establish whether the presidential interview was covered by the contract. Atiku also criticised the Presidency for presenting the recorded encounter as an interview while promoting it with photographs and a ‘coming soon’ announcement. “When Tinubu is ready for an interview, he should let Nigerians know. He cannot invite a strategist registered to work for his government, record a publicity production and advertise Sitting on a Flat Mandate as ‘coming soon’, like a trailer from 51 Iweka Road, Onitsha. “Hungry Nigerians are not here to market his failed movie. They have suffered through Part One of Tinubu’s government, and they will not sit through a sequel,” he said. The former vice president also questioned London’s professional relationship with the lobbying firm and her decision to delete social media posts in which she had praised Tinubu’s administration and Nigeria’s partnership with the United States. “After praising Tinubu’s government and Nigeria’s partnership with the United States on her social media accounts, Diana London deleted the posts. She has not explained why. Nigerians are entitled to ask what changed between the glowing praise and its disappearance,” Atiku said. He argued that the deleted posts and questions surrounding London’s professional engagements reinforced the need for the Presidency to release the complete recording. “Someone who could delete her own public praise of this government without an explanation has given Nigerians reason to wonder what will survive the editing of her interview. Will difficult questions and awkward answers remain in the final cut? Or will Nigerians be served a carefully redacted, defensive account that mutilates the facts? The Presidency can put those doubts to rest by releasing the full, unedited recording,” he said. item.title: NELFUND: I dare opposition to promise scrapping scheme — Fashola
item.description: …Says students, beneficiaries would revolt against such proposal Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged opposition politicians to campaign on a promise to scrap the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying beneficiaries and their families would resist such a move. Fashola, who spoke on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, described the student loan scheme introduced by President Bola Tinubu’s administration as one of the reforms that had eased the financial burden on families across the country. NELFUND was established in April 2024 after Tinubu signed the Student Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act into law to provide interest-free loans to eligible students in tertiary institutions. As of October 3, 2026, the fund said it had disbursed more than ₦372 billion to 1,635,676 beneficiaries across 312 tertiary institutions nationwide. Speaking at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Jigawa on November 10, Tinubu had described NELFUND as a weapon deployed by his administration to tackle poverty, insisting that the scheme would not be discontinued. Supporting the President’s position, Fashola said the initiative was introduced to help Nigerian families cope with financial obligations, particularly rent, transportation, healthcare and education. “This led to the creation of NELFUND to help families pay school fees and provide student allowances,” he said. He noted that more than one million Nigerians were already benefiting from the scheme, adding that the number was increasing. Fashola challenged opposition candidates to make the discontinuation of the programme part of their campaign promises, saying such a position would attract resistance from beneficiaries and their families. “I challenge the opponents to promise to scrap NELFUND and see how beneficiaries and their families react. They won’t dare,” he said. The former Minister of Works and Housing also addressed the rising cost of living, describing it as a global challenge whose effects were being felt in Nigeria. He called for a broader understanding of the factors contributing to the economic hardship, pointing to disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent global developments. According to him, the pandemic disrupted economic activities worldwide, forcing governments to inject money into their economies to support businesses. He said China, which he described as the world’s biggest production centre, took about two to three years to resume normal operations, contributing to supply shortages and rising prices. Fashola also identified the Russia-Ukraine war as another factor that worsened the situation, citing disruptions to the supply of energy products, including diesel, and food commodities such as wheat. item.title: Atiku’s subsidy restoration plan is ‘abracadabra’ — Fashola
item.description: …Demands figures, details on funding, crude oil supply Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has described former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore petrol subsidy as “abracadabra without proof”, challenging him to provide details of how he intends to implement the policy if elected president in 2027. Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, had in August said he would restore petrol subsidy if elected in the 2027 general elections. Fashola, who served as Minister of Power under former President Muhammadu Buhari, stated this on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He recalled that major presidential candidates in the 2023 general elections had supported the removal of petrol subsidy, questioning what had changed to warrant a reversal of that position. “For credibility’s sake, all major candidates, at least as at the last election, promised to remove this fuel subsidy. So what has changed?” he asked. Fashola said politicians advocating a different approach should explain the reasons for changing their positions and provide concrete details of how they intended to sustain the proposed arrangement. He questioned the source of funding for the subsidy, warning that its restoration could reduce allocations to state governments and undermine their ability to meet financial obligations. “I was in a government that was paying subsidy. And the states were not getting money. So we are going to go back to partial, near-zero returns, states borrowing money to pay salaries. Is that where you want us to go?” he asked. He urged voters to consider the financial implications of the proposal and use their votes to prevent a return to the revenue challenges experienced by state governments during the subsidy regime. Asked whether Atiku’s proposal was unrealistic, the former minister said he wanted detailed explanations and supporting figures before reaching a conclusion. “With the sketchy pronouncements that come with it, I want to see rigour, I want to see detail; I want to see numbers,” he said. Fashola also questioned Atiku’s argument that increased local refining would promote competition and reduce petrol prices, asking where the crude oil required to supply domestic refineries would come from. He explained that Nigeria’s crude oil production involved joint ventures and production-sharing contracts with international oil companies, meaning the country did not own all the crude produced. According to him, the assumption that Nigeria could simply supply local refineries with cheap crude overlooked the fact that crude oil was traded internationally at benchmark prices. Fashola further questioned Nigeria’s capacity to supply sufficient crude to domestic refineries, noting that the country had yet to fully optimise its production quota. item.title: Jigawa farmers-herders clash leaves three dead, two injured
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse At least three people have been killed and two others injured in a violent clash involving suspected herders and farmers in Garki Local Government Area of Jigawa State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 3:30 a.m. on Wednesday at Wauta Fulani Settlement in Rafin Marke Ward, Kanya District. The Jigawa State Command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) confirmed the incident in a statement issued on Wednesday by its Public Relations Officer, ASC Badruddeen Tijjani Mahmud. According to the corps, preliminary investigations indicated that seven suspected herders, accompanied by about 200 cattle from the Babura axis, allegedly entered a farmland belonging to 53-year-old Amadu Saleh, where the animals fed on his guinea corn crops. The statement said efforts by farmers to prevent further destruction of their crops reportedly triggered an attack by the suspected herders, who allegedly wielded cutlasses, bows and arrows. The confrontation resulted in the death of 35-year-old Amiru Saleh, while Amadu Saleh, 50, and Haruna Saleh, 37, sustained injuries. The NSCDC said another confrontation subsequently occurred after other farmers gathered at the scene, leading to the deaths of two unidentified members of the herders’ group. The surviving members of the group reportedly fled with their cattle towards Gabasawa Local Government Area of neighbouring Kano State. The corps said all the victims were taken to Garki General Hospital, where the three deceased persons were confirmed dead. It added that the remains of Amiru Saleh had been released to his relatives for burial, while the bodies of the two unidentified persons remained at the hospital pending necessary official procedures. Reacting to the incident, the NSCDC State Commandant, CC Muhammad Kabiru Ingawa, appealed to residents to avoid retaliatory attacks and refrain from taking the law into their own hands. He urged members of the affected communities to remain calm and promptly report suspicious activities or potential security threats to relevant authorities. The corps said it was collaborating with other security agencies to contain the situation and prevent further violence. It also called for peaceful coexistence among farmers, herders and other communities, reaffirming its commitment to protecting lives and property across Jigawa State. item.title: ADC, Kaduna gov’t differ over venue
item.description: From Mohammed Ibrahim Yaba, Kaduna; Hussein Yahaya, Baba Martins & Daniel Adaji, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Kaduna State Government of denying the party the use of the Ranchers Bees Stadium to host the Northwest rally of its presidential campaign. The party said it had applied to use the stadium for its rally scheduled for November 17 and 18 but was refused access to the facility by the state government, which denied the claim. The ADC National Vice Chairman, North-West, Hafsat Baba, told one of our correspondents that the party dutifully informed the state government of its intention to use the facility, but the latter turned down its request. Daily Trust reports that the All Progressives Congress (APC) recently held its presidential campaign flag-off at the same venue. In a letter dated November 12, 2026 reportedly from the Kaduna State Ministry of Local Government Affairs and addressed to the Office of the National Vice Chairman of the ADC, North-West, the ministry said the stadium would not be available on the requested dates due to ongoing repairs. The letter, signed by Mohammed Sani Haruna, Senior Special Assistant to the Commissioner, stated: “We write to acknowledge receipt of your letter with the above caption. However, we regret to inform you that due to ongoing repairs at the stadium, it will not be available for the aforementioned programme on the dates requested by you.” Baba said the ADC also notified security agencies, including the Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Inspector-General of Police, Kaduna State Police Command and the General Officer Commanding, about the planned rally. “We sent these letters not only to state security agencies but also to their national offices, just to be on the safe side,” she said. Baba explained that the party initially considered the Ahmadu Bello Stadium but was informed that it was under construction and subsequently considered the Trade Fair Complex but was also told that the facility would not be available. She said the party decided to request Ranchers Bees Stadium after learning that the APC had recently used it for its presidential campaign flag-off. “We were aware that Ahmadu Bello Stadium was under construction. We then thought of using the Trade Fair Complex, but we were made to understand that it would also not be available. We knew that they (APC) used Ranchers Bees recently, so we decided to request it, but it was denied,” she said. The ADC chieftain questioned why its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, should be prevented from holding a rally in Kaduna, which she described as his second home. “If Atiku can visit Bauchi and Yobe and hold his rallies, why can’t he come to Kaduna, his second home, because he has a house here?” she asked. item.title: 2027: Inuwa seeks royal blessings for APC candidate
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE—Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya of Gombe State has led the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, Dr. Jamilu Ishyaku Gwamna, and other party chieftains to the palace of the Bala Waja, His Highness Muhammad Danjuma Muhammad, in Talasse, Balanga Local Government Area, to seek royal blessings ahead of the 2027 general elections. The visit, which formed part of the party’s campaign engagements across the state, also provided an opportunity for the governor to highlight his administration’s achievements and ongoing development projects in Balanga. Addressing the traditional ruler, community leaders and other stakeholders, Yahaya said the decision to begin the campaign engagements in Balanga was deliberate, describing the area as home and acknowledging its longstanding relationship with his administration. He said the visit reflected his administration’s recognition of the traditional institution’s importance in governance and its commitment to seeking royal counsel and blessings while accounting for its stewardship. The governor recalled the support Balanga residents gave the APC in previous elections, saying his administration had reciprocated their confidence through investments in infrastructure and social development. He listed the construction of roads linking Balanga North and South, interventions in education, healthcare, water supply and other critical sectors as some of the projects executed to improve living conditions in the area. Yahaya particularly highlighted the restoration of electricity to Balanga after 17 years without public power supply, describing the intervention as a major achievement that had revived economic and social activities in the community. He said the electricity initiative was being extended to other communities, including Gelengu, Kaltungo, Kumo, Bajoga and Dukku, adding that 62 communities had been identified for the state’s mini-grid electricity programme. The governor also listed the establishment of Local Council Development Areas, construction and rehabilitation of schools, healthcare facilities and water infrastructure among his administration’s development interventions. On agriculture, he highlighted ongoing dam and irrigation projects, expressing optimism that the investments would boost food production, create employment and improve the economic fortunes of rural communities. He further disclosed that the State Executive Council had approved the construction of the Dalawaja-Walalunguda Road, linking Gombe State with neighbouring Adamawa State, as well as the Degri-Sikam Road. According to him, the projects would improve rural connectivity, facilitate the transportation of agricultural produce and open up communities to greater economic opportunities. item.title: Ex-Spain midfielder Juan Mata retires from professional football at 38
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Spain midfielder Juan Mata has retired from professional football at the age of 38, ending a career that brought international titles and major trophies with Chelsea and Manchester United. Mata, who won 41 caps for Spain, was part of the squad that lifted the 2010 World Cup. Two years later, he helped Spain win Euro 2012, scoring in their 4-0 final victory over Italy. The former Real Madrid youth player joined Valencia in 2007 before moving to Chelsea in August 2011. During his time at Stamford Bridge, he won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup. Mata signed for Manchester United in January 2014 and helped the club claim the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup. He left Old Trafford in 2022. He continued his career abroad with Galatasaray in Turkey and Vissel Kobe in Japan, before playing for Australian clubs Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory. Announcing his retirement, Mata said football would remain part of his life. “Football will never leave my life. There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. “I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer.” The post Ex-Spain midfielder Juan Mata retires from professional football at 38 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast against his nomination, according to US media. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. His nomination puts him on course to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as his party prepares to reverse Republican policies and investigate the administration. Jeffries must still win a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3, when he would become the first Black politician to hold the powerful post. With a large Democratic majority, this is seen as something of a formality. Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics. Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination “by acclamation” — without a formal ballot — as some allies had hoped. He argued that every Democrat should have an opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018. The ballot remained secret, with the overall tally made public but individual votes kept anonymous. Ahead of the election, Jeffries met progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare, with proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage among the topics discussed. The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party’s plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs. “Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters Tuesday. “We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.” – Brooklyn roots – Raised in Brooklyn’s working-class Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012. Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artists, he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022. item.title: Tinubu’s housing mortgage plan will enslave Nigerians with debt — Gbadamosi
item.description: By Henry Obetta The Lagos State Deputy Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Mr. Babatunde O. Gbadamosi, has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s housing mortgage initiative, describing it as an attempt to enslave Nigerians with debt. Gbadamosi, reacting to Tinubu’s announcement of housing financing programmes under the N1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund, MREIF, said the proposed monthly repayment of N85,400 was unaffordable to Nigerians earning the national minimum wage of N70,000. The two remarks were made on X, formerly Twitter, yesterday. Tinubu had said eligible Nigerians could access mortgages of up to N100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent, with repayment periods of up to 20 years and an initial deposit of 10 per cent. The President said the initiative was aimed at expanding access to affordable, long-term credit and helping hardworking Nigerians become homeowners. He explained that a prospective homeowner seeking to purchase a N10 million house could make an initial deposit of N1 million and repay approximately N85,400 monthly over 20 years. However, Gbadamosi questioned the affordability of the scheme, arguing that the proposed monthly repayment exceeded the current national minimum wage. “Now, considering that you are alleged to be an accountant, let’s do some accounting, shall we? “The current National Minimum Wage is N70,000. Given that your proposed monthly installment is N85,000 per month, please explain to me like a two-year-old how THIS is any type of affordable housing?” he queried. The ADC chieftain also questioned how retirees approaching the end of their working lives could sustain mortgage repayments for another 20 years, particularly with their pension earnings. “Granted that you seem to be pitching it exclusively to only those who are ‘nearing retirement’, how do you propose they find the N85,000 per month after retirement for twenty years? With their meagre pension?” he asked. Gbadamosi said his party was proposing a different approach to affordable housing in Lagos State, linking housing affordability to improved workers’ earnings. He said he and the ADC governorship candidate in Lagos State, Mr. Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, had promised a comprehensive review of public sector salaries to reflect prevailing economic realities, alongside the provision of at least 100,000 affordable housing units for residents. According to him, the proposed housing units would become affordable through improved salaries. “We have promised a minimum of 100,000 affordable Housing Units to Lagosians. They will be affordable because salaries would have been increased,” he said. Gbadamosi further criticised the Federal Government’s student loan programme, NELFUND, arguing that increased tuition fees had left many students with debts at the beginning of their adult lives. item.title: What has Pochettino won as a manager? His record as he joins Man Utd
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United with a career spanning six teams and nearly 700 matches as a manager. The Argentine will be tasked with improving the club’s fortunes after its difficult start to the 2026/27 Premier League season. United appointed Pochettino on Friday to replace Michael Carrick. He is expected to join the club after completing his duties as United States men’s national team coach. Here are key records and achievements from Pochettino’s managerial career: 1. Three trophies with Paris Saint-Germain Pochettino won all three of his major trophies during his time at PSG: the 2020 Trophée des Champions, the 2020-21 Coupe de France and the 2021-22 Ligue 1 title. He joined the French club in January 2021 and worked with high-profile players including Lionel Messi, Neymar and Kylian Mbappé. 2. Took Tottenham to the Champions League final Pochettino led Tottenham to their first UEFA Champions League final in 2019. Spurs lost 2-0 to Liverpool in Madrid. He also guided the north London side to three consecutive top-three Premier League finishes between 2015 and 2018. Tottenham finished second in 2016/17 with 86 points. 3. Southampton’s best Premier League finish at the time Before joining Tottenham, Pochettino took Southampton to eighth place in the 2013/14 Premier League season, matching the club’s best finish in the competition at the time. He was appointed by the Saints in January 2013 after starting his senior managerial career at Espanyol in Spain. 4. Managed 685 matches across six teams Figures published by Transfermarkt show Pochettino has managed 685 matches, winning 337, drawing 146 and losing 202. His overall win rate stands at 49.2 per cent. His six teams have been Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States men’s national team. 5. Led the US to the 2026 World Cup round of 16 Pochettino took charge of the United States in September 2024, replacing Gregg Berhalter after the team’s group-stage exit from the Copa América. Under his leadership, the US reached the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, recording the country’s most wins at a single edition of the tournament. The Americans also reached the 2025 Gold Cup final. Pochettino now faces the task of improving Manchester United’s fortunes. The club were 18th in the Premier League after taking eight points from their opening 10 matches of the season. The post What has Pochettino won as a manager? item.title: Kompany resumes work at Bayern after recovery from illness
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has resumed work after being hospitalised with meningeal irritation and is expected to return to media duties ahead of Friday’s Bundesliga match against Cologne. According to AFP, the 40-year-old is scheduled to meet the press on Thursday after returning to Bayern’s training ground earlier this week. Vanguard reported that Kompany collapsed while watching a training session on October 23 and was taken to hospital, where he was diagnosed with meningeal irritation. He was later discharged to recover at home, while assistant Aaron Danks led the team during his absence. Kompany was visibly unwell and walked with a limp during Bayern’s 6-1 win over RB Leipzig in mid-October. He was also a doubt for the Champions League match against Arsenal four days later, but took charge of the 2-2 draw before his collapse. His return to the training ground marks a gradual resumption of duties. Bayern have not indicated that he has fully resumed his role, but his scheduled press conference comes ahead of the Cologne fixture on Friday. item.title: Nigerian Army is winning war against insurgency – COAS
item.description: The Chief of Army Staff, Lt Gen Waidi Shaibu, says the Nigerian Army is recording significant successes in the counter-insurgency operations across the country. Shaibu stated this at the maiden edition of the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps (NAAC) Biennial Conference, Reunion and Pulling Out Ceremony, on Wednesday in Bauchi. The theme of the conference is “Emerging Trends in Tank Warfare for Enhanced Counter Terrorism and Counter Insurgency Operations in Nigeria”. He said that the army was making significant progress in the counter-insurgency operations in all the geopolitical zones. “We are certainly on track and focused. The NAAC remains a key player in the fight against insurgency, banditry, kidnappings among other forms of insecurity challenges across the nation, with remarkable successes,” he said. Shaibu tasked the corps to sustain the good work in synergy with other corps and security agencies to defeat security challenges bedevilling the country. He said the biennial conference marked another milestone in ensuring that the Nigerian Army paid greater attention to the sharing of knowledge, especially from the fountain and pool of retired senior officers for its advancement. The army chief described the biennial conference as one of the several initiatives aimed at encouraging the NAAC to contribute its quota toward discussing critical issues affecting the NA and suggesting viable solutions. “This event comes at a time when our involvement in several operations across the country has brought to fore the need for ingenuity, adaptability and a long-term approach to deal with the security threats which have also evolved,’’ he said. “This Biennial Conference and Reunion is therefore designed to provide us with contemporary approaches to solve our operational challenges,” he said. According to Shaibu, the conference will focus on gaining insights from participants’ experiences to improve planning, training and conduct of operations against myriads of security concerns and evolving threats facing the country. He said that the outcomes of the conference would better inform the army towards strengthening its fighting power. While commending President Bola Tinubu for his support, Shaibu urged the NAAC and other corps to use this strategy to reform the conduct of reunion by drawing extensively from the pool of knowledge from retired officers for the benefit of the army. Maj.-Gen. item.title: Gaming Phenomenon ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Goes Live After 13-Year Wait
item.description: After 13 years of waiting, including two delays and several leaks, the first gamers began playing Wednesday the latest instalment of “Grand Theft Auto”, the most expensive — and among the most profitable — video game ever developed. “GTA VI” becomes available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at midnight Thursday in each region where it will be available. That meant it launched first in New Zealand (at 1100 GMT on Wednesday), with many players around the world changing their console location settings to the far-eastern country to be among the first to enter the new Vice City. “I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time that the anticipation for this is crazy,” Australian student Riley Fennel told AFP ahead of the launch. Although Rockstar Games, the studio behind GTA, has not yet released advance unit sales figures, specialist firm Sensor Tower estimates they have already surpassed 15 million. That would be more than $1.5 billion in revenue before the game even came out, for a budget estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion, which would be unprecedented. According to the British analytics firm Omdia, sales of “GTA VI” could reach $3.2 billion by the end of the year. An organiser fixes a poster of the video game ‘Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI’ ahead of its launch party in Chennai on November 17, 2026. Photo by R.SATISH BABU / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ “No other concert or box office release has ever generated that much capital. And so that makes it one of the outliers in entertainment,” said Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” the industry specialist said. Rockstar’s parent company, US publisher Take-Two Interactive, has rolled out a massive marketing campaign to establish the title as a mass cultural product that transcends the boundaries of video games. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said James McWhirter at Omdia. “I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning this first game session “for a very long time”. Like him, many fans have already booked time off to immerse themselves in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida. The human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 percent increase in leave requests around the world for November 19. Touted as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, “GTA VI” follows the adventures of a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in the Miami-inspired, crime-ravaged Vice City. Since its beginnings, the series has won players over with its increasingly realistic reconstructions of fictionalised cities and the great freedom of action offered in a highly detailed open world. item.title: State Police: Senate Directs NASS Clerk To Transmit Amendment Bill To Tinubu For Assent
item.description: The Senate has directed the clerk to the National Assembly to transmit the Constitution alteration bill providing for the establishment of State Police to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The upper chamber has also asked the Executive to forward the National Policing Bill to the National Assembly for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage to establish the operational framework for subnational policing. The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, during plenary today. Policemen at the Niger State Police Command (Photo by Abdullahi Egba/Channels TV) In its deliberations, Senator Bamidele recalled that the National Assembly had processed an executive bill seeking to amend the 1999 Constitution to establish state police as part of Nigeria’s national policing structure. He noted that both chambers overwhelmingly approved the proposed amendment, with the Senate passing the bill on June 24, 2026, and the House of Representatives following suit on July 23, 2026, securing the constitutionally required two-thirds majority. The bill was subsequently transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for approval in line with Section 9(2) of the Constitution. The Senate Leader noted that the Senate confirmed that all 36 state legislatures had now endorsed the proposed amendment and transmitted their resolutions to the National Assembly. Having satisfied the constitutional requirements under Sections 9(1) and 9(2), the Senate maintained that the amendment had fulfilled the conditions necessary for its passage. The upper chamber therefore urged the Executive to submit the National Policing Bill to provide the legal and operational framework for the implementation of State Police. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, announced on Monday that all 36 State Houses of Assembly had approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The clerk described it as 100 per cent approval by the state legislatures, as the approval exceeded the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. “The Clerk to the National Assembly wishes to announce that all the thirty-six (36) State Houses of Assembly have approved ‘A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for related Matters’. “This represents one hundred percent (100%) endorsement by the State Houses of Assembly, which exceeds the threshold of twenty-four (24), provided under Section 9(2) of the Constitution (as amended),” Ogunlana had stated. The development marked the completion of the state assemblies’ consideration of the proposed amendment, following weeks of legislative engagement over the establishment of state police. item.title: ‎CP Azare Charges Newly Promoted Officers On Discipline, Commitment To Duty
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Commissioner of Police, CP Baba Azare, has charged the newly promoted senior officers of the Command to live up to the demands of their new ranks and justify the confidence reposed in them. ‎CP Azare gave the charge when he decorated the officers with their new ranks at the Command headquarters, Ikot Akpanabia, Uyo, on Monday. ‎The newly promoted senior officers were decorated with new ranks following their recent promotion by the Police Service Commission. ‎The Police Commissioner, who congratulated the officers on what he acknowledged as their well-deserved promotions, described their elevation as recognition of their dedication, professionalism, hard work and commitment in the discharge of their duties. ‎“Promotion comes with higher responsibilities and more expectations. You are therefore charged to justify the confidence reposed in you through greater commitment to duty, professionalism, respect for human rights and strict adherence to the rule of law.” CP Azare advised. ‎The promoted senior officers comprise three Chief Superintendents of Police (CSPs) namely: CSP Richard Oguntola, CSP Magret Alapa, CSP Bokima Bassey, three Superintendents of Police (SPs) namely: SP John Mamodu, SP Glory George, SP Victor Lane and two Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSPs) namely: DSP Emmanuel Ayoka and DSP Godwin Awana. ‎CP Azare commended the Police Service Commission for the timely promotion of deserving officers, noting that such a gesture would further boost morale and inspire more commitment among officers. ‎The Commissioner also expressed gratitude to the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, for his visionary leadership, support and sustained commitment to the welfare of officers of the Nigeria Police Force. ‎CSP Richard Oguntola, responding on behalf of the newly promoted officers, expressed appreciation to the Almighty God for His mercy and grace to witness another memorable achievement. ‎He also expressed gratitude to the Police Service Commission and the Inspector-General of Police for finding them worthy for promotion. ‎CSP Oguntola particularly thanked CP Azare for his exemplary leadership, encouragement and support, which he stated had positively impacted their career progression. ‎He reiterated their commitment to the professional discharge of the constitutional duties of the Nigeria Police Force in their respective areas of responsibility in line with international best practices. ‎The decoration ceremony was attended by members of the management team, officers of the Command, families, friends and well-wishers who joined in celebrating the officers on their well-deserved promotions. ‎ ‎ The post ‎CP Azare Charges Newly Promoted Officers On Discipline, Commitment To Duty appeared first on Channels Television .
